title: The Dark Origin Story Behind "Rule Of Thumb" Is Actually False
description:
You've probably heard where the phrase "rule of thumb" supposedly comes from. That story isn't true -- here's what etymologists have actually found.

#shorts #idioms #etymology #didyouknow

scenes.text: You've probably heard that "rule of thumb" comes from an old law letting a man beat his wife with a stick no wider than his thumb. That law never existed.
Historians and etymologists have searched for it. No such law has ever turned up in any legal record, anywhere.
The claim actually only started spreading in the 1970s, when it got repeated in legal and academic writing about domestic abuse -- and from there, it was treated as settled fact.

The real origin is much older, and far more ordinary. The phrase shows up in print as early as the 1600s, describing using your thumb as a rough, practical measurement -- close enough, without needing exact tools.
So the actual story here isn't dark at all. It's an ordinary measuring phrase that somehow picked up a completely invented, disturbing backstory three centuries later.
Had you heard the wife-beating version before, and were you surprised the law behind it never actually existed?
